courses.name: Calculus with Applications, First Course
courses.description: Develops differential calculus, limits, differentiation techniques and applications, with an introduction to integration and logarithmic/trigonometric functions.
courses.prerequisites: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Students with Advanced Placement Credit should contact the department. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 2 units for Math 3A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams. Repeat Comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2A, then Math 3A can be taken as a legal repeat as long as students get a qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam to take Math 3A.

category_review.locator: Full current2026–27course description
category_review.rationale: The complete description teaches mathematical theory and methods.

courses.name: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
courses.description: Develops integral calculus, integration techniques, sequences and series, with mathematical and physical applications.
courses.prerequisites: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Students with Advanced Placement Credit should contact the department. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 2 units for Math 3B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam. Repeat Comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2B, then Math 3B can be taken as a legal repeat.

courses.description: Studies linear equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality.
courses.prerequisites: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.

courses.description: Studies first- and second-order differential equations, systems, nonlinear equations and stability.
courses.prerequisites: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.

courses.description: Develops multivariable and vector calculus, including vector-valued functions, double/triple integrals and changes of variables.
courses.prerequisites: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.

courses.description: Introduces foundational AI techniques and interdisciplinary applications through faculty seminars, readings and discussion.

courses.description: Develops intermediate Python programming through object-oriented design, runtime analysis, data structures and software testing.
courses.prerequisites: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: CMPSCW 9 is the online version of CMPSC 9

courses.name: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Develops Python programming and data-analysis workflows for AI, covering acquisition, cleaning, transformation, simulation, visualization and statistical inference through projects.
courses.prerequisites: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).

category_review.locator: Full rendered 2026–27 catalog course description
category_review.rationale: Programming, algorithms and data preparation/analysis are the described foundations; an AI application setting alone is not model-training content.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
courses.description: Introduces discrete mathematics through counting, sets, graph theory, elementary probability and number theory.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.

category_review.locator: Full rendered 2026–27 catalog course description
category_review.rationale: The complete description is a discrete mathematical methods inventory.

courses.name: Logic and Automata
courses.description: Introduces propositional and predicate logic alongside formal languages, automata and Turing-machine models of computation.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science 41; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

category_review.locator: Full rendered 2026–27 catalog course description
category_review.rationale: Logic is paired with explicit computational theory, languages and automata rather than a general mathematics survey.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Introduces probability and statistics, including conditional probability, Bayes rules, random variables, moments, Markov chains and hypothesis testing.
courses.prerequisites: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.

category_review.locator: Full rendered 2026–27 catalog course description
category_review.rationale: The source describes mathematical probability/statistical methods rather than an engineering application survey.

courses.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Analyzes data structures and graph traversal, including correctness proofs, hash tables, heaps and balanced search trees.
courses.prerequisites: CMPSC 40 or CMPSC 41 or MATH 8 with a grade of C or better; CMPSC 24 or CMPSC 25 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139 (may be taken concurrently with CMPSC 130A); open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only. The Recommended Preparation field also lists PSTAT120AorECE139(concurrent allowed); the prerequisite field independently includes the same requirement.

courses.description: Studies algorithm design and complexity using divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming methods, recurrence analysis and NP-completeness.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A.

category_review.locator: Full current2026–27course description

courses.name: Mathematics of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Develops statistical, linear-algebra and optimization foundations for AI, including estimation, graph probability models, gradient methods, convex optimization, kernels and backpropagation.
courses.prerequisites: Math 4A; CMPSC 25 or CMPSC 24; and ECE 139.

category_review.locator: Full rendered 2026–27 catalog course description

courses.description: Introduces intelligent agents, heuristic search, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine and reinforcement learning, and responsible AI.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A and PSTAT 120A

courses.description: Studies machine-learning techniques including neural networks, concept and decision-tree learning, genetic algorithms, Bayesian and analytical learning.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Computer Science 111.

courses.description: Studies deep-learning principles, convolutional/recurrent/Transformer/graph architectures, loss design, training and inference with analysis and implementation.
courses.prerequisites: CMPSC 165B.

requirements.title: University and senior residence
requirements.summary: Register for at least three terms. A regular quarter (including the full summer period) with six resident units counts as one term; a UC summer with two to fewer than six counts as half. Complete 35 of the final 45 units in the degree-awarding college. Other institutions and UC Extension do not supply residence credit.

requirements.title: Senior EAP/UCDC residence exception

requirements.title: Three graduation GPA tests
requirements.summary: At least 2.0 separately in graded UC work, all UC major courses, and upper-division UC major courses. UC Extension is excluded except UCSB concurrent enrollment from Fall 2000. Graded incompletes enter the final calculation as F; remedial workload credit does not enter GPA.

requirements.title: Entry writing timing and credit restrictions
requirements.summary: Finish entry-level writing by the end of the third enrolled quarter or further enrollment is blocked. Writing 1, 1E or LING 12 requires C or better; unsuccessful attempts repeat in successive quarters. After matriculation, another institution cannot satisfy this requirement. Area A credit is permitted only after entry writing is satisfied. Current catalog placement/AWPE qualifications are recorded separately.

requirements.title: American History and Institutions
requirements.summary: Satisfy through an approved four-unit course, AP American History or American Government and Politics score of at least 3, a departmental noncredit exam, or the page’s listed SAT II American History score of at least 650. Equivalent accredited, UC Extension or summer coursework may qualify; prior satisfaction at another UC transfers. Nonimmigrant visa holders may petition for waiver. Approved courses may overlap GE and major requirements. Historical exam routes do not assert current test availability.

requirements.title: Applicable curriculum year
requirements.summary: Normally use the curriculum from entering UCSB as an engineer. Changing majors uses the curriculum then in force. For students admitted from Fall 1997, breaks totaling at least nine non-summer quarters require a newer year. A year change may also be petitioned.

requirements.title: Letter-grade requirements
requirements.summary: Major courses inside and outside Engineering require letter grades. At graduation the page specifies at least 120 units, or two-thirds of UCSB resident units, letter graded; preserve this wording rather than infer a new maximum/minimum formula.

requirements.title: ECE and mathematics prerequisite grades
requirements.summary: ECE prerequisites require C− or better. Progression through MATH 3A–B, 4A–B and 6A–B requires C or better. Course-specific requirements may also apply.

requirements.title: Current catalog entry-writing alternatives
requirements.summary: Before entry: AP English, Seminar or Research at least 3 (Seminar/Research award no transfer units); ACT ELA at least 30; SAT at least 680; IB higher English A at least 5 or standard English A1 at least 6; C or better in composition meeting Area A1; or CWP placement into Writing 2. AWPE is accepted only from students transferring from another UC campus, a qualification missing from the college overview.

requirements.title: Domestic and multilingual writing placement
requirements.summary: Students not placed into Writing 2 take Writing 1 and earn C or better, repeating after lower grades. Nonimmigrant international students use the multilingual diagnostic; placement may be LING 3A, 3B, 3C or 12, or Writing Program referral. LING 12 at C or better satisfies entry writing. These placements are not a requirement to take all listed courses.

requirements.title: Transfer credit, GPA and duplication
requirements.summary: Determine intended degree use before enrollment elsewhere. Non-UC courses can supply unit/subject credit but do not enter UC GPA; other UC grades do. Existing UCSB credit at D− or higher normally prevents duplicate external credit. An F permits external subject/unit credit but non-UC work does not replace the original UC GPA grade.

requirements.title: Community-college transfer limits
requirements.summary: At most105 community-college quarter units transfer; later courses may earn subject credit only. All community-college credit is lower division even if its UCSB equivalent is upper division. California community-college articulation uses ASSIST; individual course suitability is not inferred from this general rule.

requirements.title: Other UC repeat authorization
requirements.summary: Another UC course can be an authorized repeat for UCSB C− or lower when the offering department verifies identical material. Mathematics equivalencies for other UC courses from Summer2019 are stated to apply automatically, including repeat coding. Regular-term study at another UC needs advance advising and is rarely approved; summer enrollment follows its own process.

requirements.title: Concurrent enrollment and GE writing
requirements.summary: Domestic students in regular status can enroll concurrently elsewhere without college approval; academic-notice students need prior approval, often denied. International students need OISS approval. The general transfer page limits special-subject writing to UCSB; the separately reviewed petitions page expressly permits up to two approved UCEAP exceptions.

requirements.title: Repeat eligibility and GPA calculation
requirements.summary: Repeat only C−,D+,D,D−,F or NP. Major courses still require letter grading; NP cannot replace an earlier letter grade in GPA. Third enrollment needs prior college approval. Credit counts once and every grade stays on the transcript. For the first16 repeated units only the latest letter grade counts in GPA; beyond16 both attempts count. Second attempts after W do not consume the16-unit allowance. Cross-UC equivalency must be approved before repetition; identify repeats at registration.

requirements.title: Minimum cumulative progress table
requirements.summary: Regular-quarter minimum enrollment is12units. Published completed-unit targets by MCP quarter: 1: 12, 2: 27, 3: 42, 4: 56, 5: 71, 6: 86, 7: 101, 8: 116, 9: 132, 10: 148, 11: 164, 12: 180. Thresholds are progress targets, not additional degree-credit requirements.

requirements.title: MCP entry pathways
requirements.summary: First-year admits count only post-matriculation units for MCP; earlier AP/IB/college credit can still count toward graduation. Transfers entering with90–105units start at MCPquarter7 and count transferred units. Transfers below90or above105start at quarter1 and count units after first UCSB enrollment, including the immediately preceding UCSB summer.

requirements.title: MCP deficit review
requirements.summary: Two consecutive MCP deficits can trigger an academic-notice contract; two further consecutive deficits can make the student subject to dismissal. An exception needs appropriate college approval; dismissal is not inferred automatically from an observed unit count.

requirements.title: Enrollment quarter and unit limits
requirements.summary: Expected graduation within12regular quarters for first-year admits or9for junior transfers, and no more than215units. Pre-high-school-graduation credit, including AP/IB, is excluded from215. Summer does not consume regular quarters but its units count. Non-summer outside study after leaving can reduce available UCSB quarters proportionally. Further enrollment requires specific approval and a complete Proposed Schedule for Graduation; exceptions are limited.

requirements.title: Academic notice and review
requirements.summary: Cumulative UC GPA below2.0 automatically triggers notice. The college may also act on major/upper-major GPA below2.0 or inadequate major progression. Meet advising in the first two weeks, obtain an approved schedule and enrollment agreement, and undergo end-of-quarter review.

requirements.title: Disqualification thresholds and appeal
requirements.summary: Subject to disqualification after any quarter GPA below1.5, quarter GPA below2.0 while on notice, or cumulative UC GPA still below2.0 after two notice quarters. Advisors and Associate Dean review whether to continue notice or dismiss; thresholds do not mean automatic dismissal. Appeal requires Academic Self Assessment and Study Plan by the stated individual deadline. Regular-term reentry after dismissal requires reinstatement on notice.

requirements.title: MCP countable work and exceptions
requirements.summary: MCP can count repeats of C−/D/F, courses passed by examination, IP work, and passed summer courses at UCSB or transferable accredited institutions. Exceptions to minimum progress require dean/designee approval for special circumstances.

requirements.title: GE transfer substitution and EAP writing exception
requirements.summary: Transferable courses may be petitioned for general areas A/D/E/F/G and special Ethnicity/World Cultures/European Traditions with a syllabus. The special writing requirement is UCSB-only except up to two UCEAP courses may be petitioned. An already-articulated or clearly eligible transfer/EAP course may not need a petition after advising confirmation. This petition cannot turn an unapproved UCSB course into GE: UCSB GE requires Academic Senate approval.

requirements.title: Second repeat approval
requirements.summary: Third enrollment requires a rationale and study plan, is rarely approved, and carries an expectation of B or better. A major-course repeat needs both major and college approval; GE needs college approval. Cross-UC legal repeats require departmental equivalency evidence before taking the course and the legal-repeat petition after completion.

requirements.title: Excess and deficit enrollment approval
requirements.summary: Excess approval is needed above21units, or16on academic notice, after Pass2 enrollment with an accurate Pass3 plan; scheduling conflicts are not approved. Below12units needs deficit approval for documented medical/family circumstances, at least20hours weekly employment while in good standing and on-time graduation plan, or the final quarter. International students use OISS reduced-course-load approval instead. Permanent/multiquarter deficits are generally not approved.

requirements.title: Late enrollment and grade-option changes
requirements.summary: Late adds/drops or grading-option changes require exceptional circumstances and review. Poor performance, changing interests/major or workload are not late-drop grounds; weeks8–10/retroactive requests receive greater scrutiny. Grade-option petitions apply only to optional-grading courses, never letter-only courses. A late graduate-course add also needs the signed undergraduate-in-graduate-course petition. Final add/drop decisions belong to the Associate Dean.

requirements.title: American History waiver qualification
requirements.summary: F1/J1 or other nonimmigrant students who do not intend to remain permanently in the US may petition for an AHI waiver through Graduation Matters; the waiver is not automatic.

requirements.title: Double-major and extension approvals
requirements.summary: Two Engineering degrees cannot be double majors. A cross-college double major requires receiving-major advising and a study plan. A plan for enrollment beyond12first-year/9transfer quarters or215units must account for all remaining requirements; incomplete or incorrect plans are denied. Approval is not guaranteed.

Instructor approval and a course approval code permit adds after the fifth instructional day through the add deadline; the page does not say that such a late-add code overrides a major restriction.

Eligible numbers are200–299and500-level GroupStudies/SpecialTopics; other500-level courses are unavailable. The stated300–499bachelor-credit prohibition is specifically LettersandScience, so it is not generalized to Engineering.

requirements.title: Quarterly enrollment completion and study load

Register at least one course and resolve blocks by the15thinstructional day to avoid lapsed enrollment. Undergraduate full-time minimum12units; Engineering/LettersandScience maximum21units in good standing or17on probation. These are quarterly enrollment limits, not extra degree credits; late/retroactive enrollment and late course changes follow the published college processes.

requirements.title: Current general-subject scope and catalog cutoff

Areas B and C are expressly Letters and Science only. Additional approvals after the catalog cutoff may appear in GOLD; this is a published-catalog snapshot, not a live registration guarantee. The general page’s Engineering Area A2 list omits Writing105AI and the explicit online W variants included by the current Engineering-specific page; preserve that source-list difference rather than infer an exclusion or identity equivalence.

requirements.title: Certified IGETC and Cal-GETC routes
requirements.summary: The current university GE policy applies to all undergraduate colleges and expressly links Engineering. California community-college transfers with IGETC or Cal-GETC fully completed before matriculation and certified by the college satisfy the GE program. Partial certification may qualify when no more than two courses are lacking; the source literally names IGETC areas1–6 while discussing both patterns, so the receiving college determines completion of the partial program. The separate IGETC-for-STEM route permits at most three missing courses, one each in areas3,4,6, with certification and college consultation. Do not extend this STEM clause to Cal-GETC or infer a waiver of major or other university requirements.

requirements.title: Engineering special designations and petition scope

Quantitative Relationships is Letters and Science only. Writing entails at least1800 non-exam words and substantial assessment weight. The special page’s permission to petition up to two other UCSB courses is expressly Letters and Science only, not an Engineering substitution rule; Engineering’s separately reviewed UCEAP petition exception remains distinct. Special designations overlay general areas rather than add seven disjoint courses.

requirements.title: General-area nonreuse and permitted overlaps
requirements.summary: For Engineering and Letters and Science, a major course may also satisfy GE, and a GE course may simultaneously satisfy American History and Institutions. A course bearing multiple general-area designations A–G may apply to only one such area. Multiple listed memberships therefore represent alternatives, not permission to count one course in two general areas.
